rows.title: Today · signed in, there is one page and nothing to do
rows.note:
Drawn from /terminal under a real session (TerminalShell.svelte + the placeholder).

• The rail lists 1 page (Overview). The page is a heading, one sentence and a link to the synthetic demo.
• Actions with your own data: 0.
• Adding a filing takes a developer page (/dev/upload) and 5 steps: create a company, create an upload, send the file, finalize, start extraction.
• Nothing tells you what a PDF is. The upload needs a company chosen first and never asks if it's an annual report or quarterly results.

Yardstick: pages you can reach 1 → 8; steps to add a filing 5 → 1 drop plus 1 check.

rows.title: A · Every page has a door
rows.note:
Bet: the terminal looks finished from day one. The rail lists all eight R1 pages; each unbuilt one says 'Soon' and opens its own coming-soon page with a still sketch (a crate of share certificates for Holdings).

Upload lives in the Documents library. Drop a file and a row appears; when Maester has worked out what it is, the row stops at 'Needs your check' and opens to show what it read and the page it read it from. Nothing is read until you say yes.

Edge (A3): when Maester can't tell, you say what it is and pick the company.

Cost: 8 coming-soon pages, ~8 small still drawings, a library ledger, a classify step and a confirm endpoint. Least new play; the sketches never move.

rows.title: B · The intake desk
rows.note:
Bet: speed. Maester doesn't wait for you. It works out what the file is and carries on reading; the 'slip' shows what it read it as, the page it found it on, and a Change link beside each line. Changing anything reads it again.

Play: each coming-soon page has a sketch you can play with. On Holdings, drag the crane's load down; it won't land, because the walls are still going up. Direct manipulation only, nothing moves on its own (DESIGN.md §6).

Edge (B3): a presentation is kept with the company, not read.

Cost: a stage ladder component, the slip, ~8 interactive drawings (the most drawing work). Risk: a wrong guess costs a wasted read.

rows.title: C · Blueprints
rows.note:
Bet: show, don't promise. Each coming-soon page is a pencil blueprint of the page to come, annotated in hand lettering ('no price yet? it says —, never 0'), under construction tape. It sets expectations and invites feedback.

Upload asks one question as the page heading: 'Is this Harbour Cements' annual report for 2025–26?' The cover page sits beside it with the evidence boxed and numbered; each answer points at its box. Nothing is read until you say yes.

Edge (C3): quarterly results for a company you haven't added; yes adds it.

Cost: a first-page image of the PDF (rendered in the browser or by the server), ~8 blueprint drawings, the question layout. Strongest on trust: the product's own rule applied to the classification.

rows.title: Shared · the states every upload owes
rows.note:
Every direction carries these. Each says what happened and what to do; state is words, never colour. 'You left the page' is a state too: nothing stops.

The 50 MB limit is the API's real limit today and is stated before you pick a file (UI spec §8).

shared:
In every direction

• The rail lists the R1 pages, grouped as in UI spec §2: Overview, Holdings · Research, Watchlist, Documents, Analyst · Activity, Settings. R2 and later (Transactions, Performance, Alerts, Reports) never appear.
• This bends a rule: DESIGN.md §7/§10 and UI spec §2 say not to show menu items for pages that don't exist. The change: a page that doesn't exist yet may appear only as a 'Coming soon' page that says what it will do, what it needs first and offers one real action.
• Every coming-soon page: the page name as h1, a 'Coming soon' tag, one primary action ('Upload a filing'), and a demo link where the demo has that page.
• Upload: a drop zone and a 'Choose a file' button (drag is never the only way), the limit stated first, leaving the page never cancels.
• Classification always shows where it came from (a page and the words on it). Never a confidence percentage.
• Three kinds: annual report, quarterly results, other company document. Plus 'not sure', where you say.

Backend asks (all directions): upload without picking a company first; a 'work out what it is' step returning kind, company, period, statements found, each with a page; a confirm-or-change call; extraction only for annual reports and quarterly results. B also needs 'read again' on change.

All names, files and figures are synthetic.
questions:
Open questions

1. Should Maester wait for your yes before it reads the statements (A, C), or carry on and let you correct it (B)?

2. Your third kind of PDF: did you mean other documents from the company (presentations, notices), or documents not from the company at all (a broker's report)? I drew 'other company document', plus 'not sure'.

3. Where should a signed-in investor land: Documents (the one page that works) or the Overview's coming-soon page?
